results.instruction:
You love classic programming languages and vintage code. While browsing through an 
old university archive, you discovered a fascinating physics simulation written in 
Fortran 77 back in 1995. The code implements a 1D wave equation solver, and you 
really want to run it and see it work.

There is one problem: it was written for g77, an old Fortran compiler that does 
not exist anymore. Your modern Linux system only has gfortran. You need to port 
this code to work with the modern compiler.

## Location and Files

The code is located at /app/legacy_sim/ with these files:
- main.f - The main program written in Fortran 77
- data_io.f - Handles reading input and writing results
- compute.f - The physics simulation implementing the 1D wave equation
- Makefile.old - Original build file that uses g77
- input.txt - Simulation parameters

## Your Tasks

1. Create a new Makefile that works with gfortran:
   - Replace the g77 compiler with gfortran
   - Add appropriate compiler flags for compiling old Fortran 77 code
   - Name the output binary "simulation"
   - The Makefile must compile all three .f files and link them together

2. Fix any compilation errors that arise when building with gfortran:
   - The code uses old-style Fortran 77 syntax
   - You may need to use specific compiler flags
   - Get a clean compile with no errors

3. Run the simulation successfully:
   - Execute ./simulation from the /app/legacy_sim directory
   - The program should read parameters from input.txt
   - The program must complete without crashing
   - The program must create an output file named "results.dat" in /app/legacy_sim

## Success Criteria

Your solution must satisfy all of these requirements:
- A Makefile exists that uses gfortran (not g77)
- The code compiles without errors using your Makefile
- A binary named "simulation" is created in /app/legacy_sim
- The simulation binary is executable
- Running ./simulation completes without errors
- A file named "results.dat" is created in /app/legacy_sim
- The results.dat file contains valid numerical data
- The results.dat file contains exactly 1000 data lines (one per grid point)
- The final energy value in the output is between 0.01 and 100.0
- The final momentum value in the output is between -1.0 and 1.0

## Input File Format

The input.txt file contains three numeric values on separate lines:
- Line 1: Number of grid points (integer)
- Line 2: Time step for simulation (floating point)
- Line 3: Number of iterations to run (integer)

Example:
```
1000
0.001
500
```

## Output File Format

The results.dat file will contain:
- Header lines starting with # describing the simulation parameters
- Lines with "Final Energy:", "Final Momentum:", and "Final Temperature:" values
- Numerical data lines with two columns: position (0.0 to 1.0) and wave amplitude

## Important Notes

- Do NOT modify the Fortran source code files (main.f, data_io.f, compute.f)
- Do NOT change the physics algorithm
- Do NOT change the input or output file formats
- Focus only on creating a working Makefile and getting the code to compile and run
- Modern gfortran may require specific flags for old Fortran 77 code
- The simulation should complete in under 30 seconds
